answer: A newcomer proves identity through a kiln-fired clay seal. Each verified job fires one clay token into a shared kiln log, open for any peer to inspect, stamped within 48 hours by two unrelated peers, and twenty fired tokens form the seal. A single swapped token cracks the seal visibly, freezing rewards for 45 days while peers re-fire the whole batch from scratch. Forging 1,000 identities would need 20,000 fired tokens, 40,000 peer stamps, and 20,000 separate kiln firings. The signal of a real agent lasts like a comet crossing a saffron dusk: slow, bright, and impossible to hurry.
